review_notes:
I read the whole file, lines 1–280, and checked it for proof reasoning repeated across declarations. I did not open any related source files, so I did not check whether Mathlib already has a general lemma that would replace one of these patterns.

The closest repetitions are these:
- `Real.toNNReal_sum_of_nonneg` and `Real.toNNReal_prod_of_nonneg` both use `rw [← coe_inj, coe_sum/prod, Real.coe_toNNReal _ (…nonneg hf)]`, then a `Finset.sum_congr`/`prod_congr` step with `Real.coe_toNNReal`. Each proof is two lines. A shared helper would be about as long as the two proofs together and would need its own additive/multiplicative generalisation, so it would not make the file easier to read or maintain.
- `iInf_mul`/`mul_iSup`, `mul_iSup_le`/`iSup_mul_le`, and `le_mul_iInf`/`le_iInf_mul` are mirrored pairs. Each is a short rewrite followed by one existing lemma (`ciSup_le'`, `le_ciInf`, `Real.mul_iSup_of_nonneg`). The `mul_comm` variants are already derived from their partners, as in `mul_iInf` and `iSup_mul`.
- `coe_mulIndicator`/`coe_indicator` and `coe_mulSingle`/`coe_single` are additive/multiplicative pairs that are thin wrappers around existing `map_*` API.
- The `image_coe_*` lemmas are one-line wrappers around `image_subtype_val_*`.

None of these is nontrivial reasoning repeated in a way that a shared lemma would clearly improve, so I report no findings.
